dedupe_keys.name: saice infrastructure report card for south africa 2006 to 2022

description: The South African Institution of Civil Engineering has published four Infrastructure Report Cards for South Africa, in 2006, 2011, 2017 and 2022, all offered as PDF downloads on its report card page. The 2022 card (60 pages, ISBN 978-0-6397-4193-2) grades 32 subsectors of infrastructure, up from 29 in 2017, on a five-point scale from A (world class) through B (fit for the future), C (satisfactory for now) and D (at risk of failure) to E (unfit for purpose), with plus and minus signs for robust or fragile grades and shaded bars showing changes since 2006. With a few exceptions (pipelines and ICT), only publicly owned infrastructure is covered, including state-owned companies such as Eskom and concessions such as toll roads. The overall grade fell to D in 2022, the lowest recorded, after D+ in 2006, C- in 2011 and D+ in 2017; only three subsectors improved while twelve deteriorated. Access is free; the copyright notice lets the information be reproduced with clear reference to the report card. Caveats: grades are expert judgements, not measured data, and the method is described in the report, not as a dataset. Coverage is South Africa. It supports resilience and capacity planning studies that need a view of the condition of multi-sector infrastructure; the related record is the ASCE Infrastructure Report Card.
